content:
Apple today released the all-new M6 chip, part of the next-generation chip architecture, which will debut in the A20 Pro powering the iPhone 18 Pro. Below are the key performance upgrades for the iPhone 18 Pro revealed by the M6.

The M6 reveals that the iPhone 18 Pro paired with the A20 Pro will deliver significant gains in performance and power efficiency

Although the September launch event is still some time away, Apple today surprised us with two new products: the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. (Available for pre-order starting today: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)

The Mac mini features Apple's next-generation M6 chip, which belongs to the same chip family as the A20 Pro that will be used in the iPhone 18 Pro.

The following is the official introduction from Apple's press release:

The M6 adopts the most advanced 2-nanometer manufacturing technology, achieving higher transistor density on a smaller die area, delivering a leap-forward upgrade in performance and power efficiency. The M6 also debuts a dual 16-core Neural Engine, with peak computing capability up to 2 times higher than the previous generation, enabling faster on-device AI workflows. ...The M6 adopts a brand-new 12-core CPU architecture, with two more cores than the M5, consisting of 2 super cores, 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores, delivering the world's fastest single-threaded performance, and up to 1.2 times improvement in multi-threaded performance compared to the M5

The overall performance of the M6 will surpass that of the all-new A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro, which is a common characteristic of Mac- and iPad-class M-series chips.

However, since the M6 and A20 Pro belong to the same chip family, the upgrades announced for the M6 are expected to be reflected in the A20 Pro as well.

Most notably, the A20 Pro will adopt the new 2-nanometer process that Apple has been emphasising, which delivers a "leap-forward upgrade in performance and power efficiency" — one of the key selling points of the M6.

The industry has long expected that the transition to the 2-nanometer process would bring larger-than-usual performance gains, and the M6's spec details confirm exactly this.

The A20 Pro's CPU and GPU core counts may not be identical to the M6's, and the configuration of the dual 16-core Neural Engine also remains to be confirmed. However, thanks to the 2-nanometer technology, it should deliver significant improvements in the two areas Apple emphasised today — performance and power efficiency.

The exact year-on-year improvement figures are difficult to determine at this point, but when the iPhone 18 Pro officially launches in a few weeks, performance and power efficiency will be the key upgrade areas for the A20 Pro.
